resources.string: Show the car in Home Assistant: battery, charging, climate on and off, lights, and events for your automations (charging done, alarm, car home). Google Home and Alexa can then use it through Home Assistant. It uses MQTT: Home Assistant\'s Mosquitto add-on, or a broker on this bridge.
Update the bridge to connect the car to Home Assistant (Settings → Updates).
In Home Assistant the car is the device “%1$s” — Settings → Devices & services → MQTT.
Looking for brokers on your network…
No broker found on the bridge\'s network. Enter one below, or let the bridge run one.
With Home Assistant\'s Mosquitto add-on, use a Home Assistant user made for the car (Settings → People → Users).
The bridge can run one itself (Mosquitto, with a password). Takes about a minute, and the bridge needs internet for it.
Run a broker on the bridge
Setting up the broker on the bridge…
Connect Home Assistant to the bridge
In Home Assistant: Settings → Devices & services → Add integration → MQTT, and enter:

In Home Assistant: Settings → Add-ons → Add-on store → Mosquitto broker → Install, then Start. Make a user for the car (Settings → People → Users), then pick Home Assistant above and enter that user here. Home Assistant finds the broker by itself.

Share the car from Home Assistant: Settings → Voice assistants → Expose, and pick the car\'s switches, e.g. Climate. Then you can say “Hey Google, turn on %1$s Climate”. This needs Home Assistant Cloud, or Home Assistant\'s own Google Assistant or Alexa setup.
Charging finished, alarm, car home, car away and more come in the car\'s “Car event” entity — use them as triggers. Other systems (Node-RED, openHAB, Homey) can use the MQTT topics under %1$s/.
Connected — the car is in Home Assistant now.
Turned off — the car has been taken out of Home Assistant.
